title: Privacy and Error Handling knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Privacy and Error Handling”?
options: Privacy and Error Handling helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Privacy and Error Handling means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Privacy and Error Handling removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Privacy and Error Handling should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Privacy and Error Handling helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Privacy and Error Handling is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Avoiding sensitive logs” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Avoiding sensitive logs” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Avoiding sensitive logs” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Avoiding sensitive logs” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Avoiding sensitive logs” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Avoiding sensitive logs” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Avoiding sensitive logs” under Privacy and Error Handling. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Privacy and Error Handling”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
